children: AI agents could start monetizing the traffic they direct to travel booking platforms in the long term, Deutsche Bank analysts say in a note. If that happens, AI agents wouldn't be a substitute for online travel platforms like Expedia and Booking, as some investors have worried, the analysts say. Instead, agents would be "more like another performance marketing channel," they say. Additionally, travel platforms have important leverage, given they could choose to restrict bot access to inventory, pricing or booking functionality, they say. The platforms' loyalty programs and direct traffic are still key, too, they say. "Net-net, we continue to view AI as a structural watch item rather than an immediate estimate driver," they say. (kelly.cloonan@wsj.com)
